boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named Malvern-area destinations on practical corridors from Immaculata, each with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Courts and open lawn
cards.subtitle: First & Warren Avenues corridor
cards.notes: Bring a ball or use the trail connection near Massacre Run; the borough lists courts, a field, open lawn, and volleyball space.
cards.short_summary: A compact active-recreation stop beside First and Warren.
cards.evidence_claim: Malvern Borough lists baseball/softball, basketball courts, volleyball space, open lawn, and trail access at Horace J. Quann Memorial Park.
cards.source_title: Parks and Open Space | Malvern Borough
cards.access_notes: The borough says its parks are open to the public during daylight hours unless posted otherwise.

cards.title: A gazebo-side pause
cards.subtitle: East Broad Street & Old Lincoln Highway corridor
cards.notes: Use the benches, gazebo entrance, or picnic area for a short daylight break along the East Broad and Old Lincoln Highway corner.
cards.short_summary: A fenced neighborhood park with seating and play space.
cards.evidence_claim: Malvern Borough identifies Theodore S.A. Rubino Memorial Park at East Broad Street and Old Lincoln Highway with a gazebo, benches, playground, and picnic amenities.
cards.source_title: Parks and Open Space | Malvern Borough
cards.access_notes: The borough says its parks are open to the public during daylight hours unless posted otherwise.

cards.title: An outdoor hoop stop
cards.subtitle: Bridge Street & Old Lincoln Highway corridor
cards.notes: Pack a basketball for the open-air court at the Bridge Street and Old Lincoln Highway corner; use only during posted park hours.
cards.short_summary: A named public basketball court on the Old Lincoln Highway corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Malvern Borough describes John & Marion Herzak Memorial Park as a public basketball facility at Bridge Street and Old Lincoln Highway.
cards.source_title: Parks and Open Space | Malvern Borough
cards.access_notes: The borough states that the court is open to the public daily during posted park hours.

cards.title: Read the landscape trail
cards.subtitle: Monument Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the three-quarter-mile self-guided trail and pause at the interpretive panels; keep bicycles out of the battlefield as borough rules require.
cards.short_summary: A Revolutionary War landscape with a signed self-guided walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Malvern Borough says Paoli Battlefield Historical Park has walking trails, self-guided tours, interpretive signage, and historic monuments.
cards.source_title: Parks and Open Space | Malvern Borough
cards.access_notes: The borough describes the walking and jogging trails as open to the public throughout the year.

cards.title: History beside playing fields
cards.subtitle: Monument Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Combine a daylight walk with the grounds’ monuments, gazebo, picnic tables, and recreation facilities; respect the walled gravesite and memorials.
cards.short_summary: A 23-acre historic grounds with memorials and recreation facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Malvern Borough lists baseball fields, tennis courts, playground, pavilion, gazebo, picnic tables, and war memorials at Paoli Memorial Grounds.
cards.source_title: Parks and Open Space | Malvern Borough
cards.access_notes: The Borough identifies the site as a community recreational and civic space; visit in daylight and follow posted rules.

cards.title: A preserve-side walk
cards.subtitle: Willistown Greenway corridor
cards.notes: Use the preserve as a quiet daylight walk and follow the borough rule prohibiting bicycles, except mobility-assistive devices, within the preserve.
cards.short_summary: A named nature preserve in Malvern Borough’s open-space network.
cards.evidence_claim: Malvern Borough includes Randolph Woods Nature Preserve in its parks and open-space system and prohibits bicycling there except for mobility-assistive devices.
cards.source_title: Parks and Open Space | Malvern Borough
cards.access_notes: The borough says its parks are open to the public during daylight hours unless posted otherwise.

cards.title: A gazebo for civic programming
cards.subtitle: South Warren Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Check the town calendar before heading to the South Warren Avenue gazebo; the library has hosted all-ages story time at this named park.
cards.short_summary: A Malvern park used as a setting for library programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Malvern Borough’s calendar lists an all-ages Malvern Public Library story time at the gazebo in Burke Park, 16 South Warren Avenue.
cards.source_title: Malvern Public Library's Storytime @ Burke Park | Malvern Borough
cards.access_notes: Confirm any event registration and current park conditions through the borough before visiting.

cards.title: Books and local programs
cards.subtitle: East First Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Browse the library’s books and digital-media offerings or check its program calendar; it is located in Borough Hall on East First Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A public library stop inside Malvern Borough Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Malvern Borough says Malvern Public Library, at 1 East First Avenue, offers books, digital media, programs, and events for all ages.
cards.access_notes: Borough-listed hours are Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–noon and 1–6 p.m., and Friday 9 a.m.–noon; verify before travel.

cards.title: A Lancaster Avenue meal stop
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Plan a breakfast or lunch stop at the diner’s 352 Lancaster Avenue location; check its official daily schedule before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A named diner directly on the Lancaster Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Classic Diner’s official Malvern page lists its location as 352 Lancaster Avenue, Malvern, and publishes daily opening hours.
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours are daily from 6:30 a.m.; weekday closing is 2 p.m. and weekend closing is 3 p.m.

cards.title: A Carnegie Boulevard supply run
cards.subtitle: Carnegie Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Use the Malvern store’s pickup option for a planned supply run, or browse its grocery, pharmacy, and general merchandise departments in person.
cards.short_summary: A named retail stop with store pickup, grocery, and pharmacy services.
cards.evidence_claim: Target’s official Malvern store page lists 455 Carnegie Boulevard and identifies store pickup, a CVS pharmacy, and a Starbucks Café.
cards.access_notes: Check the official store page for the current daily schedule and department-specific hours before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Immaculata ceremonies and recurring class traditions, from first-year ivy to the senior Christmas procession.

cards.title: Carol Night
cards.subtitle: Villa Maria Rotunda • annual December tradition
cards.notes: Attend the candlelit carol gathering in the Villa Maria rotunda; the university calendar lists Carol Night for December 4, 2026.
cards.short_summary: A university Christmas observance of candlelight and song dating to 1921.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata identifies Carol Night as its oldest and best-loved tradition and says it has been held every year since 1921.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled on the university’s 2026–27 academic calendar for December 4, 2026; confirm event details with the university.

cards.title: The Seniors’ Lantern Entrance
cards.subtitle: Part of Carol Night in the Villa Maria rotunda
cards.notes: Watch for the seniors’ lantern-bearing entrance, which begins Carol Night ceremonially as “The Wassail Song” is sung.
cards.short_summary: A senior-led lantern procession opens Immaculata’s annual Carol Night.
cards.evidence_claim: The university states that seniors enter the rotunda carrying lanterns and that this entrance is the ceremonial beginning of Carol Night.
cards.access_notes: Occurs within Carol Night; participation and viewing arrangements are event-specific.

cards.title: Escorting the Infant Jesus to the Tree
cards.subtitle: A senior privilege during Carol Night
cards.notes: Notice the senior escort of the Infant Jesus statue to the base of the Christmas tree during the Carol Night observance.
cards.short_summary: Seniors place the Infant Jesus statue at the Carol Night tree.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata says seniors escort the statue of the Infant Jesus to a place of honor at the base of the tree.
cards.access_notes: Occurs as part of Carol Night; observe the university’s event guidance.

cards.title: Amethyst Day
cards.subtitle: Class pin and ring ceremony
cards.notes: If your class is scheduled, attend with family for the pin-and-ring ceremony, including the blessing and Alma Mater closing.
cards.short_summary: A university tradition in which sophomores receive pins and juniors receive rings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Immaculatan describes Amethyst Day as a university tradition dating to the 1940s, with sophomores receiving class pins and juniors class rings.
cards.access_notes: Class-year eligibility and ceremony timing are determined by the university.

cards.title: The Amethyst Class Ring
cards.subtitle: Presented to juniors at Amethyst Day
cards.notes: Treat the ring presentation as a class milestone; Immaculata’s account says rings are worn at graduation and connect students to their alma mater.
cards.short_summary: The amethyst ring links present classes to a tradition selected by the 1925 charter class.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata Magazine says the class of 1925 selected amethyst for the class ring and calls the practice a cherished tradition continuing today.
cards.access_notes: Available through the Amethyst Day class-ring process; consult the university for current eligibility and ordering details.

cards.title: Walking Through the Giant Ring
cards.subtitle: Amethyst Day procession in the Green Room
cards.notes: After the ceremony, join your class’s procession through the giant ring; this action was documented as the Amethyst Day sendoff.
cards.short_summary: Amethyst Day concludes with each participant processing through a giant ring.
cards.evidence_claim: The Immaculatan’s Amethyst Day report states that each student processed through the giant ring as the ceremony ended.
cards.access_notes: Part of the Amethyst Day ceremony for participating class years.

cards.title: Receiving Ivy Pins
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation • Alumnae Hall Theater
cards.notes: New students receive ivy pins during orientation before heading to the Planting of the Ivy on Immaculata Grounds.
cards.short_summary: Orientation pairs an ivy-pin reception with the incoming class’s planting ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata’s 2026 orientation schedule lists “Reception of Ivy Pins” immediately before “Planting of the Ivy.”
cards.access_notes: Listed for new students during the August 2026 orientation program; participation is orientation-specific.

cards.title: Planting of the Ivy
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation • Immaculata Grounds
cards.notes: Join the incoming class’s orientation ceremony on the grounds, following the ivy-pin reception and class photograph.
cards.short_summary: An incoming-class ceremony built into Immaculata’s new-student orientation schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata’s current orientation schedule includes Planting of the Ivy on August 30, 2026, following the reception of ivy pins.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for August 30, 2026 as part of New Student Orientation; intended for the incoming class.

cards.title: Rose Arbor Day
cards.subtitle: Back Campus • senior-class tree planting
cards.notes: Seniors gather on Back Campus to plant the cherry tree dedicated to their class; check Student Life programming for the next date.
cards.short_summary: A senior tradition of dedicating a cherry tree to the graduating class.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata’s event listing calls Rose Arbor Day an Immaculata senior tradition of planting a cherry tree dedicated to the class.
cards.source_title: Rose Arbor Day & Senior Picture Day
cards.access_notes: The 2026 event was organized by the SGA Class of 2026; future timing is set by Student Life and class leadership.

cards.title: 100 Nights
cards.subtitle: Annual senior-class countdown celebration
cards.notes: Mark the final 100 nights before graduation with the senior class’s dinner and celebration when your class council announces it.
cards.short_summary: Seniors gather annually to recognize their final 100 nights as Immaculata students.
cards.evidence_claim: An Immaculata Magazine interview identifies the 100 Nights Dinner and Celebration as an annual event marking seniors’ final 100 nights as IU students.
cards.source_title: Q&A with Kaleigh Dugan, Senior Class President
cards.access_notes: Organized by the senior class council; dates, format, and attendance details vary by class year.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Immaculata University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, campus-centered first-weekend sequence using named Immaculata places and recurring student-life options.

cards.title: Friday • Start with New Student Orientation
cards.subtitle: An Immaculata University transition activity
cards.notes: Use orientation as your first anchor: note the offices, people, and campus resources introduced there, then save one question to follow up on.
cards.short_summary: Begin by getting oriented to campus support and student-life opportunities.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata lists New Student Orientation among its campus-life offerings and identifies Orientation Leaders as a student leadership role.
cards.access_notes: Participation details and timing vary; confirm current orientation information with the university.

cards.title: Friday • Find Gabriele Library
cards.subtitle: Study, research, and student-support spaces
cards.notes: Make a short loop through the library, locate the circulation desk, and choose a table you could return to when you need focused work.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with individual study, collaboration, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Gabriele Library provides collaboration, support, and individual study space, along with learning and research resources for Immaculata students.
cards.access_notes: Library hours and area availability change by term; consult the library page before visiting.

cards.title: Friday • Spot ImmacuLatté Café
cards.subtitle: Inside Gabriele Library
cards.notes: Use this as a landmark while you learn the library layout; check current dining information before planning a food or drink stop.
cards.short_summary: A campus café located in Gabriele Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata's campus-locations guide identifies the ImmacuLatté Café as a location in Gabriele Library.
cards.access_notes: Purchases and operating availability are not guaranteed; verify current dining service details.

cards.title: Saturday • Check the IHM Student Center
cards.subtitle: Grill on the Hill, gaming room, and cardio gym
cards.notes: Walk through once with a classmate and note the gaming room and cardio gym so you know where to return for an easy indoor break.
cards.short_summary: A student-center destination with recreation and fitness spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The IHM Student Center contains the Grill on the Hill, a gaming room, and a cardio gym.
cards.access_notes: Facility use and dining availability may have student-access rules; check current campus guidance.

cards.title: Saturday • Pause at Back Campus
cards.subtitle: The quad between Lourdes, Nazareth, and Villa Maria halls
cards.notes: Take the path through this quad and use it as a meeting point; it is a practical way to connect several core buildings on foot.
cards.short_summary: A named campus quad used for events and outdoor gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata identifies Back Campus as the quad between Lourdes, Nazareth and Villa Maria halls and says it serves as an event space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and event setups vary; use marked paths and follow campus notices.

cards.title: Saturday • Locate the Main Dining Room
cards.subtitle: Nazareth Hall dining facilities
cards.notes: Find the dining room before you need it, then review the current campus dining options and meal-plan details at a relaxed pace.
cards.short_summary: The map-listed main dining-room location in Nazareth Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata's campus map lists the Main Dining Room in Nazareth Hall.
cards.source_title: IU Campus Map With Extended Key 2025
cards.access_notes: Dining access, menus, and payment requirements depend on current campus dining operations.

cards.title: Saturday • Ask About Intramural Sports
cards.subtitle: Recreational participation for students
cards.notes: Check the current sign-up route and try an activity that fits your comfort level; intramurals are a structured way to meet people without varsity commitment.
cards.short_summary: A recreational sports option open to students beyond varsity athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata states that it offers intramural sports for all students and that non-athletes can participate in recreational use of athletic facilities.
cards.access_notes: Registration, facility access, and offerings vary; check the current recreation schedule.

cards.title: Saturday • Browse a Student Club
cards.subtitle: Academic, cultural, service, and interest groups
cards.notes: Choose one club page that genuinely matches an interest and save its contact details; joining can wait until you know what your first weeks feel like.
cards.short_summary: Immaculata offers more than 30 student clubs and organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata says students can choose from more than 30 clubs and organizations spanning academics, advocacy, culture, arts, leadership, spirituality, and service.
cards.access_notes: Membership and meeting details are set by each organization; contact the group or Student Life for current information.

cards.title: Saturday • Watch for Welcome Back Bash
cards.subtitle: An annual Immaculata tradition
cards.notes: If it appears on the current calendar, go with a new acquaintance and use the event as a simple place to learn which campus groups are active.
cards.short_summary: A documented annual campus tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata identifies Welcome Back Bash as one of its annual traditions.
cards.access_notes: This is an annual event; confirm its current date, location, and attendance details through Immaculata.

cards.title: Sunday • Consider Campus Ministry Mass
cards.subtitle: Weekly Mass in the campus chapel
cards.notes: If this fits your practice or curiosity, check the current liturgy schedule and attend respectfully; Campus Ministry also offers reflection and service opportunities.
cards.short_summary: A recurring faith-based campus activity with chapel worship.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata states that Campus Ministry provides Mass in the campus chapel and lists weekly Mass among faith-based activities.
cards.access_notes: Mass times and locations may change; verify the current Campus Ministry schedule before attending.
